cards.text: Asa, king of Judah, is thirty-six years into his reign when trouble rolls in. Baasha, king of Israel, marches up against Judah. And he starts fortifying a town right on the border, a place called Ramah.

cards.question: Why is Baasha king of Israel fortifying Ramah?

answers.text: To block anyone going in or out of Judah
To guard his own border against Aram
To build a brand new capital for Israel

cards.text: Asa's boxed in. So he does what everybody does when they're stuck. He calls somebody and offers to PAY. And he's paying in silver and gold.

cards.question: Where does King Asa get the silver and gold to pay for help?

answers.text: The treasuries of the temple and palace
New taxes collected from the people

cards.question: Asa sends all that silver and gold out with a message. Who's it going to?
Asa tells Ben-hadad they should have a treaty like their fathers did. Then he gets to the real ask. What does Asa want Ben-hadad to do?

answers.text: Make peace between him and Baasha

cards.text: Ben-hadad takes the deal. His commanders hit Israel's cities and conquer Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim and all the store cities of Naphtali. Meanwhile Baasha is still out at Ramah stacking stones. That's like standing guard at your front door while somebody carries your couch out the BACK.

cards.question: When Baasha hears what's happening to his cities, he ___ fortifying Ramah and ___ his work.

cards.text: So now Ramah's just sitting there, piled high with Baasha's stones and timbers, and Baasha's GONE. Asa calls up all the men of Judah. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer. I know a good find when I see one.

cards.question: Asa's men haul off Baasha's stones and timbers and use them to build up Geba and Mizpah.

cards.text: Wall's gone. Border's open. I bet Asa's feeling pretty good about himself. Then Hanani the seer, a prophet, comes to see the king.

cards.question: What's Hanani the seer's problem with Asa's deal with the king of Aram?

answers.text: Asa relied on Aram and not the LORD
Asa paid Aram far too much silver
Asa never asked his officials first

cards.text: And Hanani says because of it, the army of the king of Aram has escaped from Asa's hand. I bet Asa's standing there like, "Escaped? Escaped? I PAID them!"

cards.question: Hanani reminds Asa of the vast Cushite and Libyan army. He says the LORD delivered that army into Asa's hand because Asa relied on Him.
Hanani says the eyes of the LORD roam to and fro over all the earth. Why?

answers.text: To show Himself strong for devoted hearts
To keep count of every army on earth
To find the kings who break treaties

cards.question: Hanani tells Asa he acted foolishly. From now on, he says, Asa will be at ___.

cards.text: So how does Asa take a hard word like that? Friend. Friend. Not well. He gets angry. Then he gets ENRAGED.

cards.question: What does the enraged King Asa do to Hanani the seer?
Hanani the seer is the only one in Judah who feels Asa's anger.

cards.text: Everything Asa did, from beginning to end, is written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel. The whole record. Every batch, the good ones and the burnt ones.
Then, in the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa's feet become diseased. And the disease keeps getting worse.

cards.question: Even in his illness, who does King Asa seek?

cards.text: In the forty-first year of his reign, Asa dies and rests with his fathers.

cards.question: Where in the City of David is King Asa buried?

answers.text: In a tomb he cut out for himself
In a cave his fathers had bought
In a field just outside the walls

cards.text: They lay him on a bier full of spices and blended perfumes, and they make a great fire in his honor. Forty-one years on the throne, friend. That's the end of Asa's story.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 3 quotes "Escaped? Escaped? I PAID them!", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The two right answers, "stops" and "abandons," fit either blank. "He abandons fortifying Ramah and stops his work" means the same thing, so a baker who swaps them is graded wrong for wording they haven't seen, not for the meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The setup points at Baasha's stones and timbers and then says "I know a good find when I see one." That gives away card 10's true or false answer, that Asa's men take the materials and reuse them.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The right answer is the only one that mentions the LORD. The wrong answers are about money and officials. In a Bible lesson, the right answer stands out as the obvious spiritual pick.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The statement treats Asa's oppression of some of the people as people feeling "Asa's anger." Verse 10 only says it happened "at the same time." It never links the oppression to his anger.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.
